messages:
linda_support: Heads up — customer on Next.js 13 reporting our JS SDK breaks builds after upgrading to @redwood/inference-js@1.2.4. Error from webpack: "Module not found: Error: Can't resolve './dist/index.cjs' in ...node_modules/@redwood/inference-js'". They say it worked on 1.2.3.
marco_eng: Which bundler/Node version? any stack trace beyond that line?
linda_support: Next.js (webpack 5), Node 18.15.0. Full error includes: "ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED" when importing `import { RedwoodClient } from '@redwood/inference-js'`.
jessica_sdk: Hmm... ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED usually means our exports map doesn't expose the path the bundler is trying to use. 1.2.4 changed the package layout to split cjs/esm builds. I pushed an exports map but maybe missing some fallbacks.
tim_repro: I can repro locally with esbuild too. Repro steps I used:
```
node 18
npm i @redwood/inference-js@1.2.4
node -e "require('@redwood/inference-js')"
```
-> throws ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED: '.../node_modules/@redwood/inference-js/dist/index.cjs' not exported
marco_eng: Do we have an explicit `exports` entry in package.json that maps both import and require conditions? Also check if we exported `./package.json` (some tools read package.json)
jessica_sdk: Current package.json (1.2.4) snippet I pushed:
```
"main": "dist/index.cjs",
"module": "dist/index.mjs",
"types": "dist/index.d.ts",
"exports": {
  ".": {
    "import": "./dist/index.mjs",
    "require": "./dist/index.cjs"
  }
}
```
marco_eng: That looks right at first glance. Potential pitfalls:
- Some bundlers try to read subpaths like `./dist/index.cjs` directly (not allowed if not exported)
- TypeScript's `types` isn't considered by Node's exports map; but consumers sometimes expect `./dist/index.d.ts` subpath if they import deep
- Older tools still prefer `main` or `module` fields
linda_support: Customer says error appears when doing named import (`import { RedwoodClient } from '@redwood/inference-js'`). Default vs named export mismatch?
jessica_sdk: Our ESM build uses `export default RedwoodClient` and also named export, but CJS build has `module.exports = defaultExport` shape that can cause named import issues if bundler interops are off. But that wouldn't trigger ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED — that's strictly exports map.
marco_eng: Could be that their bundler is resolving to `@redwood/inference-js/dist/index.cjs` internally (some bundlers crawl package.json and pick a path). If any tool tries to import subpath it must be exported in exports map. Quick check: do we accidentally omit `"./dist/index.cjs": "./dist/index.cjs"`? But subpath exports need to map from package root to file. Another common fix is to add an explicit `"./*": "./*"` fallback (not recommended) or export the dist files explicitly.
jessica_sdk: Proposed change (short term): extend exports map to include explicit dist subpath consumers might hit plus package.json and ./package.json mapping for bundlers that read it. Example:
```
"exports": {
  ".": {"import":"./dist/index.mjs","require":"./dist/index.cjs"},
  "./package.json": "./package.json",
  "./dist/index.cjs": "./dist/index.cjs",
  "./dist/index.mjs": "./dist/index.mjs"
}
```
But adding many dist entries is ugly. Better: make top-level entrypoint at `dist/index.*` only and ensure bundlers resolve via `.`.
marco_eng: Also add `typesVersions`/`types` top-level so TS picks up types. We already have `types` but some bundlers expect `exports` to include `.d.ts` mapping. There's an advanced pattern using conditional exports for types with the `types` condition — Node doesn't support it but bundlers/tsc might. For now ensure `index.d.ts` is reachable via top-level `types` field.
linda_support: Customer tried pinning back to 1.2.3 and build works. They need quick patch or workaround for prod.
tim_repro: Workaround for them: in Next config, add webpack resolve alias to force entry to package root, or modify imports to require the package root explicitly. Example alias:
```
resolve: {
  alias: {
    '@redwood/inference-js/dist/index.cjs': '@redwood/inference-js'
  }
}
```
Not ideal.
jessica_sdk: I can cut 1.2.5 with hotfix: revert exports to more permissive mapping and ensure we ship a small compat shim that re-exports cjs/esm in the root dist files. Also add "./package.json" export. I'll PR and bump patch.
marco_eng: Also add test in CI that runs a simple esbuild/webpack consumer to catch this. CI failure caught earlier with ESM/CJS matrix would have saved us.
ci-bot: CI run queued for branch/patch-exports (job: build-compat-tests)
linda_support: Please post PR link here and ETA for the customer. They are blocked on a release.
jessica_sdk: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-js/pull/142 — hotfix rework of exports and added compatibility tests. Planning to cut 1.2.5 in ~2 hours after green CI.
marco_eng: After release, ask customer to clear node_modules and lockfile before reinstall, sometimes lockfile pins old metadata.
linda_support: noted, I'll reply with ETA and the temporary alias workaround.
